faqs.a: Most adults do well on 5-6 cycles (7.5-9 hours). Teenagers need more (8-10 hours). If you wake refreshed and function well, your count is right.
faqs.q: How many sleep cycles do I need?

faqs.a: You probably woke mid-cycle from deep sleep. Six hours is exactly 4 cycles; 8 hours can land mid-cycle if your cycles run long. Try the cycle-aligned times above.
faqs.q: Why do I feel worse after 8 hours than 6?

faqs.q: Is a 20-minute nap better than an hour?

faqs.a: Yes - without it you would set the alarm a quarter-hour too early and wake mid-cycle. If you fall asleep slower, go to bed earlier.
Normal - everyone surfaces between cycles. Do not check the time anxiously; just let the next cycle start. Frequent long awakenings are worth mentioning to a doctor.
faqs.q: What if I wake up at night?

sleep-calculator.formula:
Bedtime = wake time - (cycles x 90 min + 15 min to fall asleep)
Wake time = bedtime + 15 min + cycles x 90 min

Example: wake at 6:30
6 cycles: 6:30 - (540 + 15) min = 6:30 - 9:15 = 21:15
5 cycles: 6:30 - 7:45 = 22:45
4 cycles: 6:30 - 6:15 = 00:15
howTo: Choose 'Wake at...' if you have an alarm time, or 'Bed at...' if tonight is fixed.
Pick one of the three cycle options - more cycles when you can.
Add the 15-minute wind-down: screens off, lights low.
Keep the same time daily, even weekends - your rhythm adapts in about a week.
keyFacts: A full sleep cycle lasts about 90 minutes: light sleep, deep sleep, then REM.
Waking mid-cycle (especially from deep sleep) causes grogginess - sleep inertia.
Most adults need 5-6 cycles: 7.5 to 9 hours.
It takes the average person about 15 minutes to fall asleep - counted in this calculator.
Deep sleep clusters in the first half of the night; REM in the second.
Consistent bedtimes beat perfect calculations - regularity trains your body clock.

sleep-calculator.quickAnswer: Sleep runs in ~90-minute cycles, and waking at the end of one feels far better than mid-cycle. To wake at 6:30, go to bed at 21:15 (6 cycles), 22:45 (5 cycles), or 00:15 (4 cycles) - each includes 15 minutes to fall asleep. Going to bed at 23:00? Set the alarm for 5:15, 6:45, or 8:15.

sleep-calculator.workedExample:
You must wake at 6:30:
1. Convert to minutes: 6 x 60 + 30 = 390.
2. 6 cycles need 6 x 90 + 15 = 555 min of bed time.
3. 390 - 555 = -165; add 1440 (one day) = 1275 min = 21:15.
4. 5 cycles: 390 - 465 = -75 + 1440 = 1365 = 22:45.
5. 4 cycles: 390 - 375 = 15 = 00:15.

You go to bed at 23:00:
1. Add 15 min to fall asleep + 5 cycles (450 min) = 465 min.
2. 23:00 + 465 min = 6:45 wake time.
